Seminar Title:

Development of a Crystal Plasticity Based Predictive Framework for Micro Scale Material Flow Behaviour and Tool Design for Complex Micro Forming Processes

Seminar Type:

Abstract:

The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI&ampML) technologies has significantly increased the demand for high precision miniature metallic micro components used in intelligent sensing systems, data driven control architectures and next generation smart devices. Micro forming has emerged as a sustainable and efficient micro manufacturing approach for producing such miniature components through mechanical deformation, offering high material utilization and scalability. The performance of micro forming processes is strongly influenced by internal material challenges (Size effect and tribological interactions) and tool design issues. internal material challenges cause two major issues: (i) size effects lead to uncertain material flow behaviour because of the limited number of grains available within the deformation zone and (ii) frictional response and tribological interactions at the tool&ampndashmaterial interface. In micro forming, different processes require different materials with different microstructures and grain sizes. Therefore, it is not possible to perform suitable experiments using the hit-and-trial method thus, a numerical simulation-based approach is required to predict micro scale material flow behaviour. The micro deep drawing process has emerged as an important micro forming technique for fabricating miniature metallic cups. However, increasing product complexity and scaling requirements necessitate advanced and precisely controlled process strategies involving multiple steps, which have not yet been fully developed.

The present research focuses on the development of an integrated numerical and experimental approach, where the design, development and experimental implementation of a multi-stage micro deep drawing (MMDD) tool setup and followed by, crystal plasticity finite element modelling (CPFEM) is used to predict material flow behaviour at the micro scale. The tool design and development of the MMDD process require high precision to improve material flow stability, dimensional accuracy and defect free product formation. The effective execution of varying step operations in MMDD is particularly challenging due to die-punch alignment issues and geometric complexities of the material. The numerical model is subsequently validated through experimental results and finally, an analytical numerical modelling approach is developed to reliably predict micro scale material flow behaviour with broader applicability to various micro forming processes. The outcomes of this study are expected to contribute to a deeper understanding and improved control of deformation behaviour in micro forming, thereby offering meaningful insights to the scientific and micro manufacturing research community.
